claims.statement: The 2023 Machinery Regulation is mandatory from 20 January 2027 and expands explicit treatment of AI safety functions, compliance-relevant software data, and cyber-safety.
A person making a substantial modification becomes the manufacturer for the affected machinery and assumes conformity duties; an ordinary change does not automatically create that role.
Technical documentation, declarations, and in some cases safety-related source code or programming logic must remain available to authorities for at least ten years.
Safexpert directly overlaps the proposed workflow through technical-documentation checklists, declarations, change tracking, traceable history, teamwork, standards monitoring, and reusable projects.
CEM4 and CEDOC provide further software substitutes for risk assessment, technical files, CE documentation, collaboration, and expert support.
Incumbent public prices show a real compliance budget but constrain an undifferentiated SaaS: products are sold from hundreds to several thousand euros, with service and expert add-ons.
Full-process machinery-safety consultancies can compile the technical file, perform tests, and support or assume formal roles, competing with the managed-service wedge.
Automatic binding of PLC/safety-program version identifiers to the handover baseline is a material uncovered gap in incumbent products.
Polish integrators will adopt a separate release layer rather than extend their current CE, PLM, or project tools.

contrary_evidence: Safexpert already covers change tracking, traceable histories, technical documentation, standards monitoring, and multi-user project work.
CEM4 offers technical-file and risk-assessment functionality at public prices below the discovery subscription hypothesis.
CEDOC includes onboarding and optional machinery-safety expert support.
Pilz and other consultancies already perform full conformity-assessment support.
The legal trigger is substantial modification, not every owner or integrator change.
